overview.heading: What is on the Wetherspoons sides menu?
overview.body:
The Wetherspoons sides menu includes chips, onion rings, [garlic pizza bread](/sides/garlic-pizza-bread), side salad and mushy peas, with cheese versions of the chips and bread. [Bowl of Chips](/sides/bowl-of-chips) is the straightforward potato option: thick-cut chips with a crisp exterior and soft centre. [Bowl of Chips with Cheese](/sides/bowl-chips-cheese) adds melting cheddar, making it a richer choice rather than a different base dish. Onion Rings (Six) offer battered onion with a contrasting crunch.

Side Salad brings iceberg lettuce, cherry tomatoes, cucumber and red onion to the selection. Mushy Peas provide a thick, soft accompaniment with a sweet, earthy flavour, particularly suited to battered fish. Garlic Pizza Bread takes a different route, using a thin pizza base with garlic and herb butter. Its cheese version adds mozzarella, so the choice between the breads is mainly about how rich an accompaniment you want.

overview.heading: How big are Wetherspoons side dishes?
overview.body:
Wetherspoons sides use different serving formats, but precise weights are not supplied for this listing. Both chip options come as a bowl, while Onion Rings (Six) gives you a stated count that is easier to divide when sharing. The garlic [pizza](/pizza) breads use an eight-inch base, offering a clearer size reference than the salad or peas. Avoid assuming that every side is equally substantial simply because it appears in the same section.

Format can help you decide what fits your meal. A bowl of chips adds a potato accompaniment, whereas garlic pizza bread introduces another bread-based element. Onion rings make sense when you want a counted portion with crunch. Side Salad offers a fresh contrast, while Mushy Peas are a softer addition. If sharing or feeding someone with a small appetite, ask the pub about the current serving rather than relying on an estimated portion.
